external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application in the web tier that receives browser traffic and puts jobs onto a message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker process that picks jobs up from the message queue and does the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A message queue receiving jobs from the web application for the background worker process.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker process and used to keep the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the web application reads its settings, including its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the worker reads its settings, including its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: access application
data_flows.description: The user's browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker process picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: database access
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The background worker process reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config. Both of those config stores hold the credentials the process needs

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: over HTTP/S across the public internet

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, database and config stores behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker process presents a non-web interface because it is a background worker that picks up jobs and does work rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process.

assumptions.assumption: The message queue and its job traffic are availability-critical because the web application depends on the queue to decouple and dispatch work.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application puts jobs onto the message queue and the background worker picks them up.

assumptions.assumption: The enqueue-jobs flow is availability-critical because it carries jobs required for the background work.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application puts jobs onto a message queue for processing.

assumptions.assumption: The pick-up-jobs flow is availability-critical because it carries jobs required for the background work.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the background worker process picks jobs up from the message queue.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the worker's database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The web application settings flow carries credentials because the web application config holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application reads settings from a config store holding its queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker settings flow carries credentials because the worker config holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker reads settings from a config store holding its database credentials.
